title: Maintain and Service Tractor System Components

lessons.title: Planning and performing a scheduled service
lessons.html:
Service intervals

Tractors are serviced by engine hours, shown on the hour meter, not by kilometres. The operator's manual lists what must be done at each interval, for example daily or every 10 hours, then at set hour intervals for oil, filters, coolant and transmission oil. Following the schedule protects the warranty and prevents breakdowns in planting and harvest season.

Preparing for the service

  1. Read the job card and the service schedule for the model and hours.
  2. Collect the correct service kit: filters, oils and parts by part number.
  3. Check service history for open items or recurring faults.
  4. Make the tractor safe and clean it if very dirty, so you can see leaks and damage.

Engine service

  • Drain engine oil warm, change the oil filter, refill with the specified grade and quantity.
  • Change fuel filters, drain the water separator and bleed the system if needed.
  • Service the air filter: replace or clean the primary element as the manual allows; replace the safety element at its interval. Check intake hoses and clamps.
  • Check coolant level and strength with a tester; inspect hoses and the radiator. Blow out radiator and cooler cores from the clean side outwards.
  • Check and adjust drive belts.
  • Check valve clearances at the stated interval.

Transmission and hydraulics

  • Check or change transmission and hydraulic oil and filters at the interval, using the specified oil.
  • Clean suction screens if fitted.
  • Check front axle and final drive oil levels.

Greasing

Grease every point on the lubrication chart: front axle pivots, steering, linkage, PTO shaft, clutch and brake linkages. Wipe nipples before greasing and replace broken nipples.

lessons.title: Inspections, adjustments and handover
lessons.html:
The inspection part of the service

A service is also a chance to find problems before they cause breakdowns. Inspect methodically and record what you find.

Inspection checklist

SystemCheck
BrakesPedal travel, equal braking, parking brake, fluid level
ClutchFree play and engagement; adjust to the manual
SteeringFree play, leaks, tie rod ends, king pins
Tyres and wheelsPressure, damage, wheel nut torque
ElectricalBattery, charging voltage, lights, instruments, warning lamps
HydraulicsHoses, couplers, cylinder seals, hitch operation
PTOEngagement, guards and shields
SafetyROPS, seatbelt, neutral start, mirrors, beacon
CabCab air filters, air conditioning operation

Adjustments

Make adjustments only to the values in the workshop manual: clutch free play, brake pedal travel, toe-in on the front axle, belt tension, valve clearances. Record values before and after.

Diagnostics on modern tractors

Connect the diagnostic tool to read stored fault codes and check for software updates as the dealer procedure requires. Reset service reminders after completing the service.

Road test and final checks

  1. Start and run the engine to working temperature.
  2. Check for leaks around filters and drain plugs.
  3. Check all fluid levels again.
  4. Test drive: gears, brakes, steering, hitch lift and PTO.
  5. Check gauges and warning lamps.

Handover

Complete the job card with hours, parts, fluids and quantities, adjustments and any faults found that need further work or a quote. Explain to the customer what was done and what you recommend, for example front tyres worn or a weeping hydraulic hose. Update the service record book or system. Dispose of oil, filters and coolant correctly.

Key points

  • Service by engine hours using the manual for that model.
  • Use the correct filters and oils by part number and specification.
  • Grease every point on the lubrication chart.
  • Inspect brakes, steering, tyres, electrics, hydraulics and safety systems.
  • Road test, recheck levels and record everything on the job card.
